lastCommit.message:
[ota-hal] OTA-1671: the armour bites back, and "fits dog" stops repeating the heading

Two of the owner's five queued items, shipped together because they are the
same object seen twice — the dog vest that already bites back, and the dog
armour rows that announce they fit a dog while sitting under a heading that
says so.

THE CHIP DELETION IS MEASURED, AND MY FIRST REASON FOR IT WAS WRONG
I first justified this by calling the chip's predicate a strict subset of the
section's. It is a subset in neither direction: the chip fires on
`itemIsDogArmor` (canonical kind OR CANONICAL tags), the heading on
`categorizeItem` (canonical kind OR RAW tags OR the DOG_GEAR name, behind a
fused-kind branch that returns first).

So I swept them instead. Across all 905 catalog names × four stored kinds the
two answers agree 3620 times out of 3620 — no divergence in either direction.
On everything a player can actually hold, the chip said exactly what the
heading above it already said, which is the owner's point word for word.

And the one shape that DOES diverge argues for the deletion rather than
against it: a fused piece stamped `uniqueStats.kind: 'armor'` that still
carries a dog_armor tag got `[fits dog]` while sitting — correctly, because
OTA-688 made uniqueStats.kind the forge's ground truth — under ARMOR. The chip
was the half that could lie. Removing it removes the only row-level label in
the pack that could contradict the section its item is filed in. ota1671 holds
both facts, and the OTA-1603 pin on the deleted chip line moves to the
behaviour it was protecting: a drifted vest still sections as dog armour.

THE BITE-BACK IS NOT THE VEST'S BITE-BACK
The dog vest (OTA-1640) always returns AETHERIC, whatever hit it. Player
armour returns the ATTACKER'S OWN damage type — the owner's call when I put
the choice to him. A fire-breather burns itself on your plate; a clawed thing
cuts itself. One field means something different every encounter, instead of
becoming a second, quieter aetheric channel that would make the vest's line
redundant.

WHY NOT NAME-DRIVEN, ONE OTA AFTER NAMES STARTED DECIDING STATS
I measured before choosing: exactly TWO of 297 catalog pieces have names that
already say they hurt what touches them (Mud-glass Scales, Mud-Claw Gloves).
Driving the sprinkle off names would have meant renaming ~30 pieces the owner
already owns, the OTA right after moving all their stats — churn on churn, for
a property the item card states plainly anyway. Names decide STATS (OTA-1670);
this is a different question, so it gets a different rule.

THE RULE IS CONTACT. You are INSIDE chest, hands and legs when something lands
on you. A cloak billows and a hood covers your head; neither is something an
attacker impales itself on. Skewed to Rare/Legendary because a Common should
not carry a rider, one in two of the eligible pool by stable hash, and the two
already-named pieces are in at any rarity because their names promise it and a
card must not lie. Result: 31 of 297 (10.4%) — Rare 17, Legendary 12,
Uncommon 1, Common 1; chest 13, hands 10, legs 8.

THE LADDER IS DELIBERATELY SHALLOW. 2 and 3, summed across worn pieces and
capped at ARMOR_REFLECT_CAP = 8, because six slots can carry this: a committed
thorn build lands near the cap rather than blowing past it, and a single piece
stays a nice rider rather than a strategy.

The payout fires only when the enemy actually landed a blow (dmg > 0) and only
when it survived it, so a corpse never takes a return hit; a kill by reflect
routes through resolveEnemyDefeat() rather than leaving an enemy at 0 HP
standing in the scene.

- app/engine/armorBiteBack.ts (new) — the rule, readable and pure.
- app/data/items/armor.json — `reflect` authored on 31 rows, agreeing with it.
- app/engine/equipment.ts — ARMOR_REFLECT_CAP, aggregateEquippedReflect().
- app/engine/crafting.ts — `reflect?: number` on the armour catalog type.
- app/state/combatResolution.ts — the return hit, in the attacker's own element.
- app/components/itemPreview.ts — the card states it: "Bites back: N damage to
  whatever hits you, in its own element".
- app/screens/InventoryScreen.tsx — the `[fits dog]` chip removed.
- __tests__/ota1671TheArmourBitesBack.test.ts — the catalog sweep + the rule.
- __tests__/ota1603TheVestKnows.test.ts — the pin on the deleted chip line
  repointed to the behaviour it guarded.
